clue.text: Meanwhile having fit about Oriental

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps around the other here

blocks.note: to be fit is to be 'in trim', in good condition
E is the abbreviation for East, so Oriental

explanation.surface: Someone throws a tantrum over an Asian rival while waiting for something else to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase IN TRIM is split open after its T to take the E, giving INTERIM.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim is the intervening period, so 'in the interim' works as an adverbial synonym for meanwhile.

clue.text: Pastoral care elicits shocking Teutonic outburst

blocks.note: outré means unconventional to the point of shocking
ach is a German exclamation

explanation.surface: A vicar's pastoral visits provoke an alarming outburst from a German parishioner.
explanation.definitionFit: Outreach is the work of an organisation, often a church, going out to support people in the community, a form of pastoral work.

clue.text: One responsible for perverting Scouts

indicators.note: perverting means twisting something out of its proper shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandal: someone in charge of a troop is accused of leading Scouts astray.
explanation.walkthrough: CUSTOS is Latin for a keeper or guardian, used in English for the custodian of something, such as a custos rotulorum, keeper of county records.
explanation.definitionFit: A custos is a keeper or custodian, the person with charge of something.

clue.text: Dump Beethoven's Fifth amid unknown music

indicators.note: Fifth points to the letter in fifth position of the composer's name
amid means in the middle of, so the earlier pieces sit inside the following word

blocks.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
the fifth letter of Beethoven
anon, short for anonymous, means of unknown name

explanation.surface: A music critic urges binning Beethoven's Fifth Symphony in favour of something obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Fifth' looks like the famous symphony, but it only asks for the fifth letter of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiphon is a short chant sung responsively, a piece of liturgical church music.

clue.text: Compiler's wrong to join Nazis in the mountains

definitions.note: a sierra is a single range, so this stands for the mountains as a group

indicators.note: in tells us the setter's mistake is placed within the stormtroopers' abbreviation

blocks.note: the compiler is the setter, who refers to himself as I; 'Compiler's' is read as 'Compiler is'
to err is to go wrong
the SA, the Sturmabteilung, were the Nazi brownshirts

explanation.surface: The setter confesses it was a mistake to side with Nazis hiding out in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiler's' expands to 'Compiler is', giving I ERR. The SA were the Nazi stormtroopers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long, jagged range of peaks, especially in Spain or Spanish-speaking America.

clue.text: Trounce 16th century backlash?

blocks.note: surface reading: a command to beat something soundly
setter's reading: the word Trounce is itself a rearrangement, a new formation, of the letters of a seven-letter word for a shop's serving surface

explanation.surface: An instruction to crush a religious reaction from the 1500s.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: TROUNCE is what you get when you re-form COUNTER, so the word on show is a 'counter re-formation'. The Counter-Reformation was the Catholic response to Protestantism.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic Church's sixteenth-century revival and reform was a reaction against the Protestant movement, a historical backlash.

clue.text: Heartless Moslem returns, clutching youngster in erotic fantasy

definitions.note: the incubus is the figure in such a fantasy, not the fantasy itself

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word is cut out
returns means the remaining letters come back the other way
clutching means holding something tightly inside

blocks.note: a Sunni is a member of the larger branch of Islam
a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of a cruel believer coming back with a child.
explanation.walkthrough: Moslem is an old spelling of Muslim; the Sunnis are the larger of Islam's two main branches.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a male demon believed to lie with sleeping women, the stuff of sexual nightmare.

clue.text: Short ordinand lost and found in fire

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the object rather than a synonym

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter
something lost is astray and disordered, so the letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; an ordinand is a candidate for the priesthood

explanation.surface: A trainee priest goes missing and is later discovered in a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, or firedog, is one of a pair of metal supports holding logs in a hearth fire.

clue.text: See 6
Artist reflecting unpromising start in weeds

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
in places one piece within the other
a reflection shows things mirrored, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: tares are weeds growing among corn, as in the parable
the first letter of unpromising

explanation.surface: A painter muses on a poor beginning among the weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Seurat was the French painter who pioneered pointillism.

clue.text: Expat re-mating abroad

indicators.note: abroad also means astray or all over the place, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Someone living overseas marries again in a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant has left their own country to settle elsewhere, as an expatriate has.

clue.text: Hooray for exam!

blocks.note: first meaning: an Italian cry of acclaim, 'long live!'
second meaning: an oral examination

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a cheer for an exam; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an exclamation of acclaim borrowed from Italian and the British academic term for an oral test.

clue.text: Visionary, for example, in calmer surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings are what encloses something, so the calming word wraps around the example

blocks.note: a soother is something that calms
say introduces an example, as in 'take a word, say, a short one'

explanation.surface: A prophet, perhaps, sits in a more peaceful setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothsayer foretells the future, a seer or prophet with visions of what is to come.

clue.text: Guardian flipped lid, embraced by queen in burned waste

indicators.note: flipped means turned over and jumbled, so the short word's letters are rearranged
embraced by means held inside the arms of the next piece
in places the combined piece within the final word

blocks.note: HM, Her Majesty, is the queen
taken as written
a cinder is the residue of burnt coal or wood

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist loses their temper, clasped by the monarch amid the ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' tempts as the British newspaper, but it is a carer. The burned-waste word is split after its first letter to take the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A childminder looks after other people's children for pay, acting as their carer and protector.

clue.text: Tear open with spike charge

blocks.note: to spike or lace a drink is to add alcohol or a drug to it
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: An attack in which flesh is ripped with a pointed weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spike' looks like a sharp object, fitting the tearing, but it is the verb for doctoring a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to cut or rip flesh so that it gapes, leaving a jagged wound.

clue.text: Initiate information in "Terminator"

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: an ender is something that terminates
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A briefing on the Terminator film begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Terminator' look like the film, but it is just one who ends things.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender is to cause or give rise to something, to set it going.

clue.text: Guitarist to turn 6 into water

indicators.note: into means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: a go is a turn in a game
VI is six in Roman numerals
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: A guitarist is told to make the clue 6 into a liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 down, but it is just the number in Roman form.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrés Segovia was the Spanish classical guitarist who brought the instrument to the concert hall.

clue.text: Fired up in what's inherited, not chosen

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
in places the turned word inside the next one

blocks.note: a fire that has been lit has been fired
genes are what we inherit from our parents

explanation.surface: A meditation on whether we are driven by our nature rather than by free choice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jews are traditionally the Chosen People, so a gentile, a non-Jew, is one 'not chosen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentile denotes someone outside the Jewish faith, who are called God's Chosen People in scripture.

clue.text: Unfinished row of unfinished housing in clay

indicators.note: unfinished means the end of the word is left off
unfinished again means the closing letters of the second word are dropped

blocks.note: a terrace is a row of joined houses
a cottage is a small house

explanation.surface: A half-built row of half-built homes made of clay.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word loses its last two letters, CE and GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is unglazed brownish-red fired earthenware, made from baked clay.

clue.text: Was Chair in Old Popular Music his raison d'etre?

definitions.text: Old Popular Music his raison d'etre
definitions.note: a description of a person, whose reason for being was rock music

blocks.note: first meaning: a chair on curved runners that tips back and forth

blocks.clueFragment: Old Popular Music his raison d'etre
blocks.note: second meaning: a 1960s British youth, rival of the Mods, who lived for rock and roll

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a band called Chair existed only to play old pop.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals dress the words up as a band name and a genre; read plainly, one meaning is a piece of furniture and the other a motorcycling 1960s rock fan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a curved-runner seat and also a leather-clad devotee of rock and roll in 1960s Britain.

clue.text: Hostility of bird turning on American

indicators.note: turning means the bird's name is turned around

blocks.note: a mina, or mynah, is a talking bird of the starling family
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A bird turns aggressively on an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places one piece after the other in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is ill will or animosity felt towards someone.

clue.text: Song to delight

blocks.note: first meaning: a part-song for unaccompanied voices
second meaning: great joy

explanation.surface: A tune meant to bring pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an unaccompanied part-song for three or more voices and also exuberant happiness.

clue.text: Firm negative about safe bet on showpiece

indicators.note: about means going round, so the negative surrounds the bet

blocks.note: Co is short for company, a firm
no is a negative reply
a cert is a certainty, a horse sure to win

explanation.surface: A company says no to a sure-fire wager on a spectacular event.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a work featuring a soloist with orchestra, written to display virtuoso skill.

clue.text: Greeting in reverse sheds light

indicators.note: sheds means the outer letters are cast off, leaving the inner run
in reverse means the kept letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the inner letters of these two words run together

explanation.surface: A backwards hello is illuminating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but its I is needed: greETING In, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire is to set it burning, which is exactly what ignite means as a verb.

clue.text: Hot stuff embodies colourless redemption

indicators.note: colourless asks us to strip the word for a colour out of the next word
embodies means gives a new bodily form to, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something spicy stands for a drab kind of salvation.
explanation.walkthrough: RED, a colour, comes out of REDEMPTION, leaving EMPTION to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is a sweet red pepper, also allspice, a spicy ingredient loosely called hot stuff.

clue.text: Catch Fitzgerald's disease

blocks.note: a rub is a catch or snag, as in 'there's the rub'
Ella Fitzgerald was the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: Someone contracts the illness that Fitzgerald had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests catching an illness, but it is a snag.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella is German measles, a contagious viral illness.
